props.gloss_en: a ship is pure [not susceptible to impurity]
the mishna: whence that a ship is pure? as it is said, 'the way of a ship in the heart of the sea' (Prov 30:19)
this teaches that [a ship is] like the sea: as the sea is pure, so a ship is pure
Chananya: we learn it from the sack -- as a sack is carried full and empty, so anything carried full and empty [is susceptible]; excluding a ship, which is not carried full
what is between them? an earthenware ship
by the one who says 'a ship in the heart of the sea', this [earthenware ship] too is in the heart of the sea -- pure
by the one who says 'like the sack', [the full-and-empty test] is for those written with the sack; but an earthenware ship [is impure] even though it is not carried full
or else [the difference is] a Jordan ship
by the one who says 'a ship in the heart of the sea', this too is a ship in the heart of the sea -- pure
by the one who says 'carried full and empty', this too is carried full and empty -- impure
R' Chanina ben Akavya: why did they say a Jordan ship is impure? because they load it on dry land and lower it into the water
a person should never withhold himself from the study hall, even for one hour
for this mishna was taught in the study hall for several years and its reason was not revealed until R' Chanina ben Akavya came and explained it
R' Yonatan: never withhold oneself from the study hall and from words of Torah, even at the hour of death -- as it is said, 'this is the Torah: a man when he dies in a tent' (Num 19:14)
Reish Lakish: words of Torah endure only in one who kills himself over it -- as it is said, 'this is the Torah: a man when he dies in a tent'
Rava: and for Chananya, is carrying by oxen called carrying? yes
there are three wagons: one made like a chair is susceptible to midras impurity
one like a bed is susceptible to corpse impurity
one of stones is pure of everything
R' Yochanan: and if it [the stone wagon] has a receptacle for pomegranates, it is susceptible to corpse impurity
there are three chests: a chest whose opening is at its side is susceptible to midras impurity
[one whose opening is] at the top is susceptible to corpse impurity
and one that comes in the [large] measure is pure of everything
the midras [of a zav] on an earthenware vessel is pure -- it is not susceptible to midras impurity
R' Yosei says: even the ship (what 'even' adds is what Rav Zevid and Rav Pappa dispute)
Rav Zevid: the baraita means -- the midras of an earthenware vessel is pure and its touch impure, and an earthenware ship is impure, as Chananya; R' Yosei says even the ship is pure, as our tanna

Rav Pappa: the baraita means -- earthenware: midras pure, touch impure; wooden: both midras and touch impure; and the Jordan ship is pure, as our tanna; R' Yosei says even the ship is impure, as Chananya
his bed is juxtaposed to him: as he has purification in a mikveh, so his bed [subject to midras] must have purification in a mikveh
the baraita: a reed mat is susceptible to impurity through a zav
R' Chanina: there [the mat] is different, since there is [purification in a mikveh] in its kind

the stam: what is the reason? two verses are written, 'and a man who touches his bed' (Lev 15:5) and 'every bed on which the zav lies shall be impure' (Lev 15:4); how so? if there is [purification] in its kind, [it is impure] though it itself has none; if not, his bed is juxtaposed to him

Rava: the midras of an earthenware vessel is pure from here -- 'every open vessel that has no sealed cover on it' (Num 19:15): with a sealed cover it is pure; are we not dealing even with one he designated for his menstruant wife, and the Merciful says pure?
Rava's criterion, read from 'every open vessel that has no sealed cover on it [is impure]' (Num 19:15): an earthenware vessel with a sealed cover on it is pure
Rava's bridge: the verse speaks even of [a sealed vessel] he designated for his menstruant wife, and the Merciful One says pure -- so an earthenware vessel is not subject to midras

schemas.gloss_en: נלמדנה משק: מה שק מיטלטל מלא וריקן אף כל מיטלטל מלא וריקן -- as the sack, so [what is written with it]: susceptible only if carried full and empty; a ship, not carried full, is excluded
ואיש אשר יגע במשכבו (Lev 15:5) -- his bed is juxtaposed to him: as he has purification in a mikveh, so his bed; an earthenware vessel, which has none, is not subject to midras
כמשכב נדתה יהיה לה (Lev 15:26) -- her bed is juxtaposed to her: as she has purification in a mikveh, so her bed; excluding an earthenware vessel, which has none
ומה פכין קטנים שטהורין בזב טמאים במת, מפץ שטמא בזב אינו דין שיהא טמא במת -- small pitchers, pure as to a zav, are impure by a corpse; a mat, impure as to a zav, surely impure by a corpse

supports.gloss_en: דאמר רבי חנינא בן עקביא: מפני מה אמרו ספינת הירדן טמאה -- מפני שטוענים אותה ביבשה (no SupportKind names דאמר)
אין, דתנן: שלש עגלות הן... של אבנים טהורה מכלום; ואמר רבי יוחנן: ואם יש בה בית קבול רמונים טמאה טמא מת -- a stone wagon is pulled by oxen, not carried, yet susceptible (no SupportKind names דתנן)
ומדרס כלי חרס מנלן דטהור? אמר חזקיה: ואיש אשר יגע במשכבו -- מקיש משכבו לו
דבי רבי ישמעאל תנא: כמשכב נדתה יהיה לה -- מקיש משכבה לה, לאפוקי כלי חרס
וטעמא מאי? תרי קראי כתיבי... יש במינו -- אף על גב דלית ליה טהרה במקוה; אין במינו -- מקיש משכבו לו
רבא אמר: מדרס כלי חרס טהור מהכא -- וכל כלי פתוח אשר אין צמיד פתיל עליו

objections.gloss_en: מתיב רבי אילעא: מפץ במת מנין... מפץ שטמא בזב... ואמאי, הא לית ליה טהרה במקוה! -- the baraita has the mat impure as to a zav though it has no purification in a mikveh

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר ליה רבי חנינא: שאני התם הואיל ואיכא במינו (= p_ika_bemino)

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה: רחמנא ליצלן מהאי דעתא -- may the Merciful save us from this view

answered_by.gloss_en: אדרבה, רחמנא ליצלן מדעתא דידך -- on the contrary, from yours; the stam then gives the reason (s_taama_mai_trei_kraei)

objections.gloss_en: מתקיף לה רב פפא: מאי אף? -- on Rav Zevid's reading R' Yosei does not add to the first tanna but disputes him, so 'even' has no sense
